title: A trust region method for noisy unconstrained optimization
contribution: Makes the classical trust-region method tolerate bounded noise by one change, a ratio test relaxed by r*eps_f in numerator and denominator, and proves that the iterates visit a critical region with ||g|| = O(sqrt(eps_f), eps_g) infinitely often and never leave a level set C2 after the first visit (read in arXiv v1).
problem_entry: The authors' own runs showed the classical TR often tolerates noise but can fail (p. 2); the ratio test is named as the component that breaks, since its numerator is O(eps_f) while its denominator is O(Delta_k) (p. 4).
key_idea: Relax both sides of the actual/predicted ratio by r*eps_f (r = 2/(1-c2)) so that rho ~ 1 still means an adequate model; all else unchanged; needs only eps_f and costs nothing extra (pp. 1-2, 4-5).
assumptions: Lipschitz gradient, errors only bounded, ||B_k|| < L_B, Cauchy decrease, f~ bounded below, no convexity (pp. 6-7); eps_f known; deterministic worst-case framework set against probabilistic analyses (p. 3).
proof_devices: Lemma 1: |rho_k - 1| bound from Taylor, noise bounds and Cauchy decrease (p. 7)

Lemma 2 / Corollary 1: the radius must grow when ||g~|| > r*eps_g + gamma and Delta <= gamma/(rM), giving a radius lower bound; the Remark marks this as the departure from classical TR theory (pp. 8-9)
Lemma 3: fixed decrease per accepted step, eta the smallest positive root of a quadratic, slack mu keeps it meaningful at zero noise, later mu = eps_g/2 (pp. 9-11)
Theorem 6: contradiction via f~ -> -infinity gives infinitely many visits to C1 (pp. 11-12)
Proposition 1 / Corollary 2: one-step increase bounded by r(1-c0)eps_f; radius bound kept by induction (pp. 12-13)
Theorem 7: excursion analysis in two cases; count l = ceil(log_nu(Delta_bar/Delta_{K+1})) regrowth iterations and bound displacement by a geometric series (pp. 13-17)
experiments: MATLAB, uniform noise (ball for g), no stop test, 200 iterations (p. 18); failure demos on an 8-D quadratic and a tridiagonal N = 200 with small Delta0 using four-panel diagnostics (pp. 18-20); noisy indefinite Hessian with identical noise in both arms (pp. 20-21); bound-scaling test over a noise grid and 10 seeds (pp. 21-22); supplement: Rademacher noise and Schittkowski problems 271, 289, 293 (pp. 25-34); no aggregate over a test set.
positioning: Extends his group's relaxed line searches [2, 27, 21] to trust regions (p. 2); neutral survey of norm-test, stochastic-SQP, probabilistic-TR and complexity work; leaves open whether deterministic and probabilistic approaches complement each other (p. 3); 10 of 27 references are his (pp. 23-24).
writing: One-change claim in the abstract and the intro's second paragraph (pp. 1-2); interpretive remarks after each lemma and theorem (pp. 7, 9, 11, 12, 17); hedges placed with the evidence (pessimistic bound pp. 19-20; classical sometimes better p. 21; single runs vary p. 22).
limits_future: Bounded noise, pessimistic worst-case bound (p. 21), claims hold only on average (p. 22), no stop test and few problems (p. 18); future: restart with reduced noise as a disciplined high-accuracy scheme (p. 23); no estimation or recovery for eps_f.

method_links.note: Classical TR kept; only the ratio test is changed, driven by an explicit noise level; failure shown first on an easy chosen problem with internal diagnostics; convergence to a noise-determined neighbourhood.
No recovery tree, re-estimation or exit flag; runs have no stop test; only an outer restart with reduced noise is sketched.
Bound plotted against runs and called pessimistic; goes beyond step 4 by also testing the bound's scaling in (eps_f, eps_g) over a grid and 10 seeds.
Identical noise injected into both arms; the unmodified method's advantage (milder oscillations) printed.
Step 7 stop rule: illustrative runs on a few problems with no aggregate profile behind them.

title: Constrained optimization in the presence of noise
contribution: Gives a convergence theory for a classical l1-merit SQP method for equality-constrained problems with bounded noise in functions and derivatives: with only the Armijo test relaxed by R = 2(eps_f + pi*eps_c), the iterates enter a noise-determined critical region C1, revisit it infinitely often and stay in a level set C2; experiments ablate the relaxation and stress the noise estimate (read in arXiv v1).
problem_entry: KNITRO runs with injected noise and noise-aware finite differences were acceptable at low noise but degraded markedly at higher noise (pp. 2-3); theory is then called essential, and the scope is narrowed to equality constraints and a simple SQP method (p. 3).
key_idea: Keep every SQP component (QP step, least-squares multipliers, classical penalty rule that at least doubles when it increases) and change only the line search to a relaxed Armijo test with margin R = 2(eps_f + pi*eps_c), which cannot fail (pp. 3-5, 18).
assumptions: Lipschitz gradients of f and c_i, bounded noise in f, c, g, J, beta_k bounds, sigma_min(J) >= gamma > eps_J, bounded sequences (pp. 5-6); noise level known or estimable (p. 2); admitted conveniences: H_k = beta_k I (p. 2), unique QP solution 'admittedly a strong assumption' (p. 5), no safeguards (p. 6), C2's supremum may be infinite (p. 14).
proof_devices: Descent lemma on the true merit function phi with linear model l(x; s) (pp. 6-7)
Range/null-space step split with Stewart's projection perturbation bound ||P~ - P|| <= eps_J/gamma (Lemma 3.4, pp. 7-8)
Model decrease for a large enough penalty and the stationarity measure psi_pi (Lemma 3.5, Corollaries 3.6-3.7, pp. 8-10)
Penalty eventually constant because increases at least double; analysis at fixed pi_bar (pp. 4, 10)
|l~ - l| <= eps_l and step-length threshold alpha_hat with halving giving alpha_k >= alpha_bar (Theorem 3.8, pp. 11-12)
Critical region C1 as the union of the failure sets of three sufficient-progress conditions; level set C2; Theorem 3.11 (pp. 13-14)
Constants unpacked: E, eps_l scale with delta = 1/(gamma - eps_J), 1/b_l, eta/b_l; with m = 0 the conditions reduce to Berahas et al. (p. 15)
experiments: Python, nu = 0.1, tau = 0.9, beta_k = 50; HS7, BT11, HS40 with uniform noise; ||x_k - x*|| over 1000 iterations (pp. 15-17); ablation of the relaxation at three noise levels and budgets 100/500/1000 (Tables 4.1-4.3, p. 18); noise estimates 10x-1000x too large or too small with a naive stop test and (opt)/(ls) markers (Tables 4.4-4.6, pp. 18-19).
positioning: Polyak, Hintermueller and Schittkowski's NLPQLP (no convergence theory) as early work (p. 3); the closest work, Berahas-Curtis-Robinson-Zhou-O'Neill stochastic SQP, is treated respectfully, and the difference (their penalty assumption, the same boundedness assumption) is stated plainly (p. 4); C1/C2 compared with Berahas-Byrd-Nocedal (p. 15).
writing: A 'Contributions of this work' subsection with the hedge beside the claim ('somewhat pessimistic bounds', p. 3); a discussion section that turns a complex region into orders of magnitude (p. 15); strong assumptions labelled as such (p. 5); final remarks open with two guiding questions and list open problems (p. 20); tables called 'Figures 4.6-4.4' (p. 19).
limits_future: Equality constraints only; Jacobian never near singular (p. 20); large constants and pi_bar dependent on x0 (p. 15); no regularization or trust region (p. 5); future: practical globalized algorithm (p. 5), local analysis with sharper bounds, stop test, singularity, nondiagonal Hessian, noisy inequality constraints (p. 20); recovery procedure needed (pp. 19-20).

method_links.note: Guiding question is the minimal modification when the noise level can be estimated; only the line search is changed; the repair is ablated (line search fails near x* without it) and the estimate is stress-tested 10x-1000x both ways.
Recovery tree named as necessary for robust implementations but not built; stop test called naive.
Started from a KNITRO failure observation; failure modes and open choices written in as next work (globalization, local bounds, stop test, singularity, nondiagonal Hessian, inequality constraints).

The version analysed is a stripped SQP (H = beta*I, unique QP, no TR or regularization), not the KNITRO code; penalty rule would not converge with a general H; no bound plotted against runs; experiments measure ||x - x*|| while the theory is in phi.
Step 7: three small CUTEst problems, no aggregate, no rival code, declared illustrative ('it suffices to test only a few examples').

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Iterates enter C1, revisit it infinitely often and never leave level set C2 (Thm 3.11); analogous level set noted in Berahas et al.

coauthors: Figen Oztoprak (Artelys), Richard Byrd (Colorado Boulder); Shigeng Sun thanked (p. 20)

quotes.text: As the noise level was increased, the quality of the solution deteriorated markedly, suggesting that classical optimization methods should be redesigned to handle noise.
What are the minimal modifications of a classical optimization algorithm that allow it to tolerate noise, when the noise level can be estimated?

title: Constrained and composite optimization via adaptive sampling methods
contribution: Extends adaptive sampling to constrained and composite stochastic problems by replacing the pointwise norm test with a look-ahead test that compares gradient variance with the length of the proximal step, proves linear (strongly convex) and O(1/k) (convex) convergence in expectation, and gives a practical inner-product variant (read in arXiv v1).
problem_entry: The norm test, the basis of adaptive sampling, fails under constraints because pointwise decisions cannot predict the quality of the projected step; shown by a one-constraint quadratic picture (abstract p. 1; Fig. 1.1, p. 2); a priori geometric growth has no guidance on its rate (p. 3).
key_idea: Accept a sampled gradient only if Var_k[g_k] <= xi*||(E_k[x_{k+1}] - x_k)/alpha||^2; implement with a trial prox step from the current sample and sample variance, resample and recompute if needed; reduces to the norm test when h = 0 by design (pp. 3, 5, 11-12).
assumptions: f [mu, L]-smooth or convex with L-Lipschitz gradient, h closed convex proper, unbiased g_k, fixed alpha = (1-eta)/L (pp. 6-8); admitted: (3.6) not enforceable in practice (p. 8), (3.10) more restrictive (p. 11), practical rule approximate (pp. 11-13), inner-product test assumes an independence that does not hold (p. 13).
proof_devices: One-step inequality evaluated at the comparison point x~ = beta*x* + (1-beta)x_k with beta = mu*alpha, which cancels the strong-convexity term (Lemma 3.2, pp. 6-7)
Q-linear rate in expectation under (3.6), which reduces to the norm test with xi = eta/(1-eta) when h = 0 (Theorem 3.3, pp. 7-8)
O(1/k) for convex f by telescoping ||x_k - x*||^2 and monotone expected values (Lemma 3.5, Theorem 3.6, pp. 8-9)
Computable condition via the bias-variance split and the measurable true-gradient prox point x^_{k+1} with prox nonexpansiveness, bounding the cross term by alpha*Var (Theorem 3.7, p. 10)
Sample-size rule from Var = population variance / S_k (Corollary 3.8, p. 11)
experiments: l1-regularized logistic regression, lambda = 1/N, six datasets (pp. 13-14); GEOMETRIC (gamma swept) vs NORM vs IP, each with the step chosen from a grid, S0 = 2, stop at 1e-8 or 100 epochs, phi* from 50,000 deterministic iterations; optimality gap against effective gradient evaluations and batch fraction against iterations, with parameter sweeps and a best-run panel; mushrooms in the main text, five datasets in Appendix A (pp. 14-26); CPU time and number of repetitions not reported.
positioning: Norm-test lineage (Carter; Friedlander-Schmidt; his own Byrd et al. 2012 and Bollapragada et al.; Cartis-Scheinberg; Pasupathy; Roosta-Mahoney; De et al.) (p. 3); inexact prox-gradient work lacks an automatic accuracy rule (pp. 3-4); a priori schedule [13] criticized (p. 3); 'N.B.' priority note on concurrent Beiser et al. (p. 3, footnote p. 4).
writing: Abstract runs motivation -> failure of the existing mechanism -> fix -> theory -> experiments (p. 1); failure picture early (p. 2); 'reassuring' collapse checks after the theorems (pp. 8, 11); candid caveats where they arise (pp. 8, 13); final remarks name the cornerstone condition and one open question (p. 14).
limits_future: Convex f only (pp. 6, 8); (3.10) more restrictive than (3.6), a less restrictive computable condition is open (p. 14); IP test without theory (p. 13); one problem class (p. 13); the step is grid-tuned in the experiments while the theory fixes alpha = (1-eta)/L, a gap not discussed (pp. 7, 14).

method_links.note: Proximal-gradient engine kept; the sample-size control that breaks under constraints is replaced by an estimate-driven look-ahead test with a built-in recovery (resample and recompute, reusing samples); failure first shown on one chosen picture.

Rival a priori schedule as baseline with a gamma sweep, the same step-size grid for every method, cost in effective gradient evaluations, all six datasets reported; but nothing handicapped on his side and the summary panel compares best runs.

The theorems cover the idealized (3.10), while the code runs its approximation (3.15) and the theory-free inner-product test; no bound against runs; standard rates do not separate NORM from GEOMETRIC.
Step 5: what cannot be proved is kept as a stated open question and an admitted heuristic.
